# Potential incidence of aerosols generated by vegetation burns on air quality in the Aburra Valley region.

The air quality in the Aburrá Valley is influenced by sources of emissions of particulate matter that are given to the interior and to the exterior of the territory. This study analyzes external sources of pollution, such as regional vegetation burns and provides elements that allow to understand the incidence of emissions produced on the air quality of a territory. Remote sensing using MODIS is used to find heat points and identify aerosols generated by such burnings, using the optical thickness product of aerosols (AD) with the multi-angle atmospheric correction algorithm (MAIAC) and the PM values detected by in situ monitoring stations. Likewise, a retrospective analysis using the HYSPLIT model was carried out to verify the origin of the contaminated air masses that arrived at the Valley between 2016-2020 and a specific analysis for the mandatory isolation time generated by the COVID19 in 2020. The results show that between February and April of the study period, the largest number of burns in the north-east Antioqueño and therefore the highest concentrations of ODA reaching values above 0.6, the concentrations of the highly contaminated and the economically inactive areas and 24.5 the inferno- and aerosols generated by those burns, by using the optical depth (AOD) aerosol with the multi-angle atmosphere correction algorithm (MAIAC) and the PM values detected by monitoring stations In situ. Likewise, a back-requestory analysis was performed using the HYSPLIT model to verify the origin of the contaminated air masses that arrived in the Abura Valley between 2016-2020, also and a specific analysis was carried out for the curve imposed by COVID19 in 2020.
